pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with CHECK; test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' asserts seeded rows are all 0 and a value of 2 is rejected.
src/index.js item() prefixes '★ ' only when starred; 'AC-2' test expects exactly ['First item','★ Second item','Third item'].
VIEWS.starred filters WHERE starred = 1 ORDER BY id; 'AC-3' stars 3 then 1 and expects id order.
'AC-4' checks '/' and '/?show=all' list all items in id order with a starred item in place.
'AC-5' checks 'Starred only' link on / and 'All items' link on /?show=starred; the state tests also check the links on the empty views.
Object.hasOwn guard returns 400 with no list; 'AC-6' tests Starred, none, empty and __proto__.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?show=starred'; 'AC-7' test asserts it. The route-check script and traffic test fake were updated to allow a query.

findings.what: AC-7 only checks that the route is listed. No test covers the traffic Worker requesting a route with a query end to end, though traffic.test.js's fake app now records the search string.
findings.fix: Optionally assert in traffic.test.js that a round requests '/?show=starred'.

lenses.note: The change matches the spec and its go; nothing was added beyond it except the traffic-check relaxation, which the AC-7 route needs and the PR discloses.
All 7 acceptance items and all 4 state-table rows have named tests. The spec has no later edits: it was added in one commit with the go dated before the work.

npm test could not run here because vitest is not installed. I judged by reading: the tests assert rendered behaviour and would fail against broken code. The fake-app change in traffic.test.js loosens nothing. The new shell test cases cover both the rejected and the accepted route forms.
The README describes ?show=starred. The traffic section already says routes come from routes.json.
Object.hasOwn guards the prototype-key case. The SQL is built only from fixed view constants, so there is no injection. HEAD requests go through the same path. No defects found.
The show value is never reflected into the page and the title is HTML-escaped. The only change to input validation is the route regex, which still refuses spaces and '#'.
The diff touches only a plain server-rendered HTML string, with no UI component or style files.
The diff touches only a plain server-rendered HTML string, with no UI component or style files.

The title and body match the diff: the migration, the 400 on other values, the routes.json entry, the traffic-check change and its tests are all as described. Claims about CI and the reviewer are not checkable from the repository.
